column3: Company decision = yes
column4: Legal name with LLC/Inc designator; name availability check result and date; state; principal office address; mailing address; registered agent name and address (self or service); organizer name and address; member-managed or manager-managed; members and ownership %; business purpose (general); effective date; filing fee from the state page; who files and how
column5: sba-state-registration; usa-state-government (the state's own .gov filing page)
column6: File it. Pay a fee. Use a non-.gov filing service without the inventor choosing it.

column3: Company decision = yes
column4: Members, contributions, ownership %, management, voting, profit and loss allocation, adding/removing members, what happens if someone leaves or dies, dissolution; note that a lawyer reviews before signing
column6: Present it as legal advice or a finished agreement.

column3: Company decision = yes (drafted then, marked "use after the state approves the company")
column4: Legal name; trade name; responsible party name (SSN/ITIN: LEAVE BLANK, inventor fills by hand on the IRS site); entity type and number of members; state; start date; reason for applying; closing month of accounting year; first wage date (if any) and expected employees; principal activity; principal product or service
column5: irs-ein (apply only at irs.gov; it is free)
column6: Store, ask for, or write any SSN, ITIN or EIN. Apply on the inventor's behalf.

column3: Company decision = yes (drafted then; each line marked for after formation)
column4: Business bank account; state tax registration if selling taxable goods; sales tax permit; local business license; BOI report only if the current FinCEN page says it applies; bookkeeping setup; annual report due date

column3: Company yes or no once selling is near
column4: Product description; where sold; units per year; price; hazards from the risk sheet; claims history (none); coverage wanted (product liability, general liability); questions for the agent
column6: Contact an agent. Buy a policy.

column3: Patent decision = yes or for now with a small step
column4: Title; inventors and contributions; date of conception and evidence; problem solved; how it works; what is new; variations; drawings list; earliest public showing or sale (dates, audience); known similar products and patents

column3: Patent road open
column4: Search date; database; search terms; document number; title; how it differs; relevance

column3: Inventor chooses to file a provisional
column4: Specification outline; drawing sheet list; cover sheet fields (inventor names, residences, title, correspondence address); entity status worksheet (micro/small: the inventor certifies, not the AI); fee from the current USPTO fee page; filing route (Patent Center account is the inventor's)
column6: File it. Certify entity status for the inventor.

column3: Requirements exist (at the agreed depth)
column4: Item/function; requirement ID; failure mode; effect; severity; cause; prevention control; occurrence; detection control; detection; action priority or RPN as chosen; recommended action; owner; target date; result; first-pass S, O and D proposed on every row and marked proposed, with one line of why
column6: Invent the AIAG-VDA tables. Hide a severe item behind a low combined score.

column3: Making or assembly steps are known
column4: Process step; function; failure mode; effect; severity; cause; prevention; occurrence; detection; detection rating; action; owner

column3: A quality item or process risk needs a check during making
column4: Part/process; characteristic; special characteristic flag; specification/tolerance (or proposed); measurement method; sample size and frequency; control method; reaction plan; owner
column6: Mark a proposed limit as approved.

column3: A requirement needs checking
column4: Test ID; requirement ID; method; sample size; conditions; acceptance criteria; equipment; who; when; result; revision tested
column6: Record a result that did not happen.

column3: A concept is chosen and has rough dimensions
column4: Print-style drawing: title block (part name, number, rev, date, drawn by 'AN Creation analyst - concept', scale, units, material, finish, tolerance note), front/top/side views, overall dimensions, key features called out, notes ('CONCEPT - NOT FOR MANUFACTURE' until reviewed); a section or detail view of the feature that makes it new, proposed proportions labelled
column6: Present a concept print as released for manufacture.

column3: A concept is chosen
column4: Concept image whose prompt names the new feature in physical terms and what it must not look like (prompt saved beside it; retry once if the feature is missing); a render from blender-template.py with PARTS filled from the drawing, checked by looking at the PNG
column6: Call a render a design or a test.

column3: Parts are named
column4: Item; part name; description; material; qty; make/buy; supplier candidate; unit cost (estimate or quote, marked); source

column3: Ready to ask for quotes
column4: Drawing revision; quantities (proto and production); material and finish; tolerances that matter; packaging; timeline; questions; supplier candidate list (from the library); NDA question if the patent road is open

column3: Two or more quotes are in
column4: Supplier; revision quoted; qty; unit price; tooling; lead time; MOQ; shipping; landed cost; notes

column3: The screening says a regime applies
column4: FCC: device type, intentional or unintentional radiator, module FCC ID, test lab, authorization path. FAA: drone weight, Part 107 or other, airspace near airports, waiver/authorization needed, remote ID. CPSC: children's product?, required tests, CPC fields. UL/NRTL: standard, lab, listing path. FDA: claim wording, classification, product code, submission type. Each with the official page and the open questions
column6: Claim compliance. Contact an agency or lab.

column3: Outside money = yes
column4: Amount; milestone it pays for; use of funds; type (loan, grant/SBIR, angels, crowdfunding, license); what the funder needs; documents needed; dates

column3: Price or channel is being chosen
column4: Customer; price; channel; claims to make and their evidence; FTC check on each claim; listing fields for the marketplace if any; barcode (GS1) need

column3: A buyer (school, store, hospital, factory, agency) is interested, or the inventor asks what paperwork buyers or safety people want
column4: Index of what this kind of buyer usually asks for, each line marked have / draft ready / not yet / not applicable with a reason: product spec sheet; assembly, use and care instructions with warnings; test reports and certificates that apply (from the screening: CPSC/CPC, UL listing, FCC ID, IP rating, load test); certificate of insurance; W-9 (EIN or SSN filled in by hand by the inventor); vendor registration (SAM.gov for federal, the district or city portal for local); warranty statement; quote on letterhead with lead time and payment terms; country of origin; SDS only if a chemical product. Ask the buyer for their own list when one exists.
column6: Send it. Fill in a tax ID. Claim a test or listing that has not happened.

column3: A concept is chosen and someone outside will see it
column4: Name and model; what it does (in the agreed claim wording); dimensions and weight (proposed or measured, marked); materials and finish; capacity or load (only if tested, else 'not rated yet'); power; compliance status (each line: tested / planned / not applicable); care; warranty; contact
column6: Print a rating that hasn't been tested.

column3: Before anyone outside the project uses one
column4: Assembly steps; intended use and users; what not to do; warnings for each severe DFMEA item (pinch, tip-over, small parts, hot, heavy); care and cleaning; age grading if children may use it; label text and where it goes
column6: Present draft warnings as reviewed by an engineer or lawyer.

column3: Always
column4: Social Security numbers, ITINs, bank and card numbers, passwords and login details are never asked for, written or stored. The form shows the field as 'you fill this in by hand on the official site'.

column3: Always
column4: Forms are prepared, never filed, sent, emailed or submitted. Web pages may be read. Nothing is purchased, registered or applied for by the assistants.
